english.title: Manufacturer / designer / importer / supplier fail to ensure safety of article when set / used etc. at work

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Health and Safety at work etc act 1974

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the

(A)_[designer]_
(B)_[manufacturer]_
(C)_[importer]_
(D)_[supplier]_

of an article

(E)_[for use at work,]_
(F)_[of fairground equipment,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..), failed to discharge your duty to ensure, so far as was reasonably practicable, that it was so designed and constructed that it would be safe and without risks to health at all times when it was being set, used, cleaned or maintained by a person at work
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(1)(a) and 33(1)(a) of, and Schedule 3A to, the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
manufacturer/designer/importer/ supplier fail to discharge
health and safety duty
as set out in detail in s. 6(1)(a) of the Act

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Proceedings for an offence shall not, in England and Wales, be instituted except by an inspector or the Environment Agency or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, see section 38 of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

consent.description: Health and Safety at Work Inspectorate

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see Schedule 3A to the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
